# State parents and levels: v5.x

Pinned origin/master: `b13783a138f9e50d2fed08005c9305f525096d2a`, fetched 19 October 2026. Only `parent_id` and `level` need changes; existing ISO types/local types remain. The 205-row ledger covers all existing states in the five requested countries and the twelve named disagreements. Source IDs resolve once in `states_parents_v5x.sources.json`, including exact-byte SHA-256, retrieval time, edition, and clauses. Serbia is excluded. The ISO mirror is a diagnostic comparison only; national law determines all proposed parents. No source coordinates, names, IDs or codes are copied or changed.

**Iceland — deliberately unlinked.** [Local Authorities Act 138/2011 of 28 September 2011, Articles 1–2](https://www.government.is/library/04-Legislation/Local%20Authorities%20Act%20No%20138_2011.pdf) places autonomous municipalities under national municipal-affairs supervision. The [government information centre](https://mcc.is/living-in-iceland/governance/authorities) explicitly identifies two government levels and dates the current count of 61 municipalities to May 2026. Thus the eight ISO landshlutar are geographical/statistical regional groupings, not a mandatory intervening government tier: preserve their null administrative level and parent. Set 61 municipality records to level 1, parent null. Hold Skagabyggð 5602, Skorradalshreppur 5603, and Tálknafjarðarhreppur 5612 because official merger evidence contradicts their standalone current identities ([municipal association, 24 June 2024](https://www.samband.is/frettir/sameining-skagabyggdar-og-hunabyggdar-samthykkt), [Borgarbyggð minutes, 4 September 2026, item 2](https://borgarbyggd.is/fundargerdir/20020), [Vesturbyggð history, merger 19 May 2024](https://www.vesturbyggd.is/stjornsysla/vesturbyggd/um-sveitarfelagid/)). No merger, rename, deletion, new scope or replacement ID is implemented here; the successor municipalities' unchanged tier does not certify their geometry.

**Indonesia — deliberately unlinked.** [Law 23/2014, promulgated 30 September 2014, Article 2(1)](https://s.mkri.id/public/content/infoumum/undang/pdf/anotasiRev_201742_2.%20Anotasi%20UU%20No.%2023%20Tahun%202014-Pemda-hyp.pdf) divides the republic directly into provinces and those into kabupaten/kota. The seven ISO geographical units are island groupings, not provincial parent administrations. Preserve all 38 existing province-equivalent rows at level 1 with parent null and all seven geographic rows at null administrative depth and parent. This country needs no data edit at the pinned base. The official annotated legal PDF was acquired 8 October 2026, rehashed here; its archive retrieval date is preserved rather than represented as a fresh download.

**Dominican Republic — linked.** [Law 345-22, promulgated 29 July 2022, gazette pages 5–19](https://abogadom.net/uploads/legislaciones/leyes/LeyNum345_22.pdf) cites constitutional Articles 12 and 195–196 establishing regions in territorial organisation; Article 6(4) identifies the intermediate tier for decentralisation/deconcentration, while Article 7 prescribes all ten regions and their provincial membership. These are statutory territorial administrative/planning units, not merely a statistical classification, even though they are not an additional elected provincial government. Set ten regions to level 1 and 31 provinces plus Distrito Nacional to level 2 with the Article 7 parent. The brief's '32 provinces and the district' overcounts: this base contains 31 provinces and one district. Article 7(10) expressly includes Distrito Nacional in Ozama; Article 7(7) puts Azua in El Valle, avoiding the older ISO/Decree 710-04 Valdesia grouping. Existing 'Higuamo' spelling and ISO region codes remain unchanged; no type/type_local correction is necessary for this scope.

**Cabo Verde — deliberately unlinked.** [Lei 48/X/2025, 4 April 2025, Estatuto dos Municípios](https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/DownloadAct?id=74660) establishes municipal autonomy and State–municipality relations; Articles 1–5, 13 and 15–21 govern this tier. The [government-hosted constitutional text, Article 227](https://www.governo.cv/documentos/constituicao-da-republica/) corroborates municipalities as local authorities, with other categories requiring legislation; this undated file is historical corroboration, not asserted as a current consolidation. Barlavento and Sotavento are geographical island groups, not administrations above municipalities. Set all 22 municipalities to level 1 with parent null; retain the two ISO geographical-region rows with null administrative depth/parent. No new regional authority is inferred from geographical membership or from constitutional permission to legislate future tiers.

**Equatorial Guinea — linked.** [Ley Fundamental, promulgated 16 February 2012, Article 3(4)–(5)](https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/pdf/Ley_Fundamental_Guinea_Ecuatorial.pdf) explicitly divides national territory into regions, provinces, districts and municipalities for administrative and economic purposes, with boundaries/names fixed by law. These are legally recognised administrative regions, so geographical character alone is not a reason to discard them. [INEGE, Guinea Ecuatorial en Cifras 2019, published 26 December 2019, printed pages 9–11](https://inege.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/Guinea-Ecuatorial-en-Cifras-2019.pdf) identifies Insular's three provinces and Continental's five, including Djibloho with Law 4/2017 of 20 June. Set both regions to level 1 and eight provinces to level 2 with the appropriate region parent. Continental is the existing Río Muni id 3438; Insular is 3442. No region rename or province boundary change is proposed.

**Philippines — existing links verified and retained.** [RA 12000, 11 June 2024, sections 3–4](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2024/ra_12000_2024.html) places Siquijor and both Negros provinces in the now represented Negros Island Region 5853 and establishes regional government offices. [EO 36, 19 September 2001, sections 2 and 4](https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2001/eo_36_2001.html) places Lanao del Norte in Northern Mindanao 1339 and Sarangani/South Cotabato in SOCCSKSARGEN 1310. [EO 91, 30 July 2025, section 3](https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2025/eo_91_2025.html) expressly assigns Sulu to Zamboanga Peninsula 1325 after its final 2024 exclusion from BARMM. [RA 11054, 27 July 2018, Article III section 2](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2018/ra_11054_2018.html) supports Basilan's Bangsamoro regional membership, excluding Isabela City; 1316 is CSC's legacy-named regional row and is not renamed in this task. Regional membership is an official administrative layer rather than just an ISO statistical grouping. All eight listed provinces already have these parents and level 2 at the pinned base; no parent fix is necessary and no stale ISO rollback is emitted.

**Morocco — existing links verified and retained.** [Decree 2-15-40, 20 February 2015, Article 2 annex, Bulletin Officiel 6340 of 5 March 2015, printed pages 1008–1010 (both memberships on page 1010)](https://pdfs.legisium.com/bo/general-edition/fr/6340_cQ62f.pdf) establishes the twelve administrative regions and enumerates their provinces/prefectures. Nouaceur belongs to Casablanca-Settat 3303 and Chtouka-Ait Baha to Souss-Massa 3295. Both existing rows already have these direct parents and level 2, so retain them. The retained evidence is the public gazette scan obtained from a legal-document mirror; it is not represented as a successful download from the SGG URLs, whose failures are in fetch_receipts.json.

**France — existing links verified and retained.** The [government answer published in JO Sénat on 2 February 2023](https://www.senat.fr/questions/base/2022/qSEQ221204654.html) explains Laws 2015-29 of 16 January 2015 and 2019-816 of 2 August 2019 and Decree 2016-1689 of 8 December 2016: Grand Est is the State administrative region; the creation of the European Collectivity of Alsace in 2021 did not remove Bas-Rhin and Haut-Rhin's State departmental prefectures. The current INSEE COG pages for [Bas-Rhin](https://www.insee.fr/fr/metadonnees/geographie/departement/67-bas-rhin) and [Haut-Rhin](https://www.insee.fr/fr/metadonnees/geographie/departement/68-haut-rhin) both give Grand Est (44) as region. Therefore these administrative departments retain direct Grand-Est parent 4820 and level 2; Alsace 4811 is a parallel territorial collectivity with departmental competences, not an extra State administrative tier. This follows ADMINISTRATIVE_STRUCTURE.md's explicit France example. Both named rows already match; inserting Alsace merely to match the mirror would be wrong.

Counts: P counts null-to-parent assignments; L counts changed level fields; F counts changed non-null parents. U counts every deliberately unlinked in-scope row, including unchanged geographical rows and municipalities whose level changes; U overlaps changed rows by design. H counts held records, disjoint from changed/verified rows. The twelve original disagreements are separately verified unchanged, not counted as F.
